title: A comparison of two Datetime units casts to the coarser
description: `Datetime("ms") == Datetime("us")` casts both sides to the coarser unit: 1.5 s as ms equals 1.5005 s as us. DuckDB compares the same pair on the timeline and gives false.
This is why a scan widens a coarser unit to microseconds once, before any operation sees two units.
reference: D61: scans read s and ms as microseconds; a microsecond and a nanosecond timestamp meet only through a written cast.

evidence.sql: DataFrame({m: 1500 as Datetime('ms'), u: 1500500 as Datetime('us')}).select(m == u, m < u)

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (Python). DuckDB 2.0.0 for `select m=u, m<u` over `TIMESTAMP_MS '1970-01-01 00:00:01.5'` and `TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:01.5005'`: (false, true).
